L26: # Attachments
L27: 
L28: A flexible, composable attachment component for displaying files, images, videos, audio, and source documents.
L29: 
L30: The `Attachment` component provides a unified way to display file attachments and source documents with multiple layout variants.
L31:

L47: ## 【53†Installation】

L49: AI Elements
L50: 
L51: shadcn CLI

L53: Manual

L55:     npx ai-elements@latest add attachments
L56: ## 【54†Usage with AI SDK】
L57: 
L58: Display user-uploaded files in chat messages or input areas.
L59: app/page.tsx
L60: 
L61:     `"use client";
L62: 
L63:     import {
L64:       Attachments,
L65:       Attachment,
L66:       AttachmentPreview,
L67:       AttachmentInfo,
L68:       AttachmentRemove,
L69:     } from "@/components/ai-elements/attachments";
L70:     import type { FileUIPart } from "ai";
L71: 
L72:     interface MessageProps {
L73:       attachments: (FileUIPart & { id: string })[];
L74:       onRemove?: (id: string) => void;
L75:     }
L76: 
L77:     const MessageAttachments = ({ attachments, onRemove }: MessageProps) => (
L78:       <Attachments variant="grid">
L79:         {attachments.map((file) => (
L80:           <Attachment
L81:             key={file.id}
L82:             data={file}
L83:             onRemove={onRemove ? () => onRemove(file.id) : undefined}
L84:           >
L85:             <AttachmentPreview />
L86:             <AttachmentRemove />
L87:           </Attachment>
L88:         ))}
L89:       </Attachments>
L90:     );
L91: 
L92:     export default MessageAttachments;`
L93: ## 【55†Features】
L94: 
L95:   * Three display variants: grid (thumbnails), inline (badges), and list (rows)
L96:   * Supports both FileUIPart and SourceDocumentUIPart from the AI SDK
L97:   * Automatic media type detection (image, video, audio, document, source)
L98:   * Hover card support for inline previews
L99:   * Remove button with customizable callback
L100:   * Composable architecture for maximum flexibility
L101:   * Accessible with proper ARIA labels
L102:   * TypeScript support with exported utility functions
L103:

L102: First time? Set up a runtime
L103: 
L104: Runtime components read their state from an assistant-ui runtime. Add one to an existing project:
L105: 
L106:     `npx assistant-ui@latest init`
L107: Then wrap your app in a runtime provider:
L108: 
L109:     `import { AssistantRuntimeProvider } from "@assistant-ui/react";
L110:     import { useChatRuntime, AssistantChatTransport } from "@assistant-ui/ai-sdk";
L111: 
L112:     export default function App() {
L113:       const runtime = useChatRuntime({
L114:         transport: new AssistantChatTransport({ api: "/api/chat" }),
L115:       });
L116: 
L117:       return (
L118:         <AssistantRuntimeProvider runtime={runtime}>
L119:           {/* your components */}
L120:         </AssistantRuntimeProvider>
L121:       );
L122:     }`
L123: The 【176†installation guide】 covers new projects, templates, and API routes.

L127:     `npx shadcn@latest add "@assistant-ui/elements-composer"`
L128: 
L129: Props-driven: no runtime or provider required.
L130: A file added to the composer becomes a chip: an icon for its kind, its name and size, and a trailing slot that carries a spinner while it uploads and a remove button once it is done. With a runtime the chip tracks a real upload through an attachment adapter; standalone you hold the list of files and their state yourself.
L131: ## 【177†Getting started】
L132: 
L133: A composer stages files the same way it stages text: `aui.composer.addAttachment(file)` adds one, an `AttachmentAdapter` turns it into a `PendingAttachment` and then a `CompleteAttachment`, and `s.composer.attachments` reflects the list at every step.
L134: ### 【178†Configure an attachment adapter】
L135: 
L136: Attachments are opt-in: without an adapter, `s.thread.capabilities.attachments` is `false` and `AddAttachment`, paste, and drop all no-op. assistant-ui ships adapters for the common cases:
L137: app/chat-provider.tsx
L138: 
L139:     `import { useLocalRuntime, CompositeAttachmentAdapter, SimpleImageAttachmentAdapter, SimpleTextAttachmentAdapter } from "@assistant-ui/react";
L140: 
L141:     const runtime = useLocalRuntime(chatModel, {
L142:       adapters: {
L143:         attachments: new CompositeAttachmentAdapter([
L144:           new SimpleImageAttachmentAdapter(),
L145:           new SimpleTextAttachmentAdapter(),
L146:         ]),
L147:       },
L148:     });`
L149: ### 【179†Add and list attachments】
L150: components/assistant-ui/elements/composer-attachments.tsx
L151: 
L152:     `"use client";
L153: 
L154:     import { ComposerPrimitive, AttachmentPrimitive } from "@assistant-ui/react";
L155:     import { PlusIcon, XIcon } from "lucide-react";
L156:     import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
L157:     import { field, ghostButton } from "@/components/assistant-ui/elements/surfaces";
L158: 
L159:     export function ComposerAttachmentsRow() {
L160:       return (
L161:         <ComposerPrimitive.Attachments>
L162:           {({ attachment }) => (
L163:             <AttachmentPrimitive.Root
L164:               className={cn(field, "flex items-center gap-2.5 rounded-[14px] py-1.5 ps-1.5 pe-2.5")}
L165:             >
L166:               <span className="max-w-36 truncate text-xs font-medium">
L167:                 <AttachmentPrimitive.Name />
L168:               </span>
L169:               {attachment.status.type !== "running" && (
L170:                 <AttachmentPrimitive.Remove aria-label={`Remove ${attachment.name}`} className={cn(ghostButton, "size-5")}>
L171:                   <XIcon className="size-3" />
L172:                 </AttachmentPrimitive.Remove>
L173:               )}
L174:             </AttachmentPrimitive.Root>
L175:           )}
L176:         </ComposerPrimitive.Attachments>
L177:       );
L178:     }
L179: 
L180:     export function AddAttachmentButton() {
L181:       return (
L182:         <ComposerPrimitive.AddAttachment aria-label="Add attachment" className={cn(ghostButton, "size-8")}>
L183:           <PlusIcon className="size-4" />
L184:         </ComposerPrimitive.AddAttachment>
L185:       );
L186:     }`
L187: `ComposerPrimitive.Attachments` is a render-prop over every staged file; `AttachmentPrimitive.Root` scopes `.Name`, `.Remove`, and `.unstable_Thumb` to the attachment at that position, so they need no index or id passed in by hand. `AddAttachment` opens a native file picker filtered to `s.composer.attachmentAccept` (the adapter's `accept`, or every file type when none is configured).
L188: ### 【180†Accept drag-and-drop】
L189: 
L190:     `<ComposerPrimitive.AttachmentDropzone className="data-[dragging=true]:border-dashed data-[dragging=true]:bg-blue-500/[0.04]">
L191:       {/* the rest of the bar */}
L192:     </ComposerPrimitive.AttachmentDropzone>`
L193: `AttachmentDropzone` sets `data-dragging="true"` while a file is dragged over it and stages every dropped file the same way `addAttachment` does; it claims the drop even without an adapter configured, so an unprevented drop never navigates the tab away to the file.
L194: 
L195: Standalone, a chip is a pure function of a `ComposerAttachment` object: nothing here uploads a file or tracks progress on its own. You own the array and mutate it as an upload proceeds.
L196: ### 【181†Hold the attachment list】
L197: app/chat-box.tsx
L198: 
L199:     `"use client";
L200: 
L201:     import { useState } from "react";
L202:     import { ComposerAttachments, ComposerAttachmentChip, type ComposerAttachment } from "@/components/assistant-ui/elements/composer";
L203: 
L204:     export function ChatBox() {
L205:       const [attachments, setAttachments] = useState<ComposerAttachment[]>([]);
L206: 
L207:       const remove = (name: string) =>
L208:         setAttachments((prev) => prev.filter((a) => a.name !== name));
L209: 
L210:       return (
L211:         <ComposerAttachments>
L212:           {attachments.map((attachment) => (
L213:             <ComposerAttachmentChip key={attachment.name} attachment={attachment} onRemove={remove} />
L214:           ))}
L215:         </ComposerAttachments>
L216:       );
L217:     }`
